solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 21 down to 24); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fly right into blow dealt with axe

indicators.note: one letter goes into the middle of the reworked letters, so 'into' places it inside
something dealt with has been handled and processed, so these words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fly is caught in the middle of an axe-swing, an unlikely victim of a lumberjack's stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' could be a verb, but it is the noun: the whole answer names an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-warble is the warble fly, whose larvae burrow under the skin of cattle and spoil their hides.

clue.text: Ten with aversion to certain insects — and salt

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a dislike of one kind of insect: hate of ants, read as ant-hate

explanation.surface: Someone who scores ten for loathing insects is also, oddly, a chemical salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The aversion is read as two words, ANT and HATE, written ant-first.
explanation.definitionFit: A xanthate is a chemical compound formed as a salt or ester of xanthic acid, used in mining flotation.

clue.text: Brief possibly pornographic song that has makings of rock

definitions.note: the answer is a single mineral; the definition is a plural phrase for what rock is made of

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter is dropped from the next word

parts.note: adult material is the usual euphemism for content that may be pornographic
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A short, racy song is said to contain the makings of a rock number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests rock music, but it is geology: the answer is a mineral found in rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Adularia is a clear variety of orthoclase feldspar, and feldspars are among the main minerals that make up rocks.

clue.text: Keen at first to have a go at climbing Highland tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run in the opposite order
at first points to the opening letter only of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of keen
to rib someone is to tease or have a go at them

explanation.surface: An eager climber is keen to tackle a tree in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Birk is the Scots word for a birch, so it is the tree as named in the Highlands.

clue.text: Rhetorical question somewhat tame to readers, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters are read backwards
somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters span the three words, starting inside the first and ending inside the last

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question strikes readers as a rather tame device when they think it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotema is the term in classical rhetoric for a question asked for effect, with no answer expected.

clue.text: Bearing old vase and vestment girl holds cross

indicators.note: the girl holds the other pieces, wrapping around them

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
O is a standard abbreviation for old
an urn is a kind of vase
an alb is a white vestment worn by a priest
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: An antique vase and a church robe are carried by a girl holding a cross, like a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: JO holds O, URN and ALB, giving JOURNALBO, and X is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal box is the housing in machinery that supports a rotating shaft's journal, so it is a type of mechanical bearing.

clue.text: Rounded characters, etc, mostly mean a large measure of intelligence

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: mean and nasty both describe unkind behaviour
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Rounded letters and the like are taken, a little unkindly, as a sign of great intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastaliq is a flowing, rounded style of Perso-Arabic script, used for writing Persian and Urdu.

clue.text: Big wheel in bird enclosure, not area having young plants

indicators.note: in places the important person inside the enclosure
not means the following piece is left out of the enclosure

parts.note: an aviary is an enclosure for birds
A is the abbreviation for area
a big wheel is an important person, a VIP

explanation.surface: An important person stands in a birdcage with no room to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big wheel' looks like a fairground ride, but it is slang for an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivipary in botany is seeds sprouting into seedlings while still attached to the parent plant, so the plant bears its young directly.

clue.text: Within one year, not prepared to back land-tenure

indicators.note: within puts the middle pieces inside the outer two
back means the whole string is read from right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
raw food is not prepared or cooked
taken as written
YR is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Within one year, someone unready for it has to return the land they hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryotwari was a system of land tenure in British India under which each peasant cultivator paid revenue directly to the state.

clue.text: Five removing cape run quietly over, uncloaked

indicators.note: removing means the next piece is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: cinque is the five at dice or cards
C is the map abbreviation for cape
R is the cricket-scoring abbreviation for run
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
O is the scorecard abbreviation for an over in cricket

explanation.surface: Five people creep away quietly without their capes, having shed their cloaks.
explanation.walkthrough: CINQUE loses its C, then R, P and O follow. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In querpo is an old phrase for being in body clothing only, without a cloak or outer garment.

clue.text: Pound, perhaps, short over time, dividing notes in threes

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the shortened name is read backwards
dividing means these pieces sit between the two notes, splitting them apart

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: short means the name is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: Ezra Pound was an American poet; perhaps signals an example of a first name
T is the abbreviation for time
ti is another spelling of the sol-fa note te

explanation.surface: A poet writes short verses in threes, splitting musical notes over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money or weight, but it is the poet Ezra Pound. One word, notes, gives both TE and TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Terzetti is the plural of terzetto, an Italian musical term for a trio, a piece for three performers.

clue.text: Peeler's half dislodging plug in nut plant

indicators.note: dislodging means pushing something else out and taking its place
half means only the first half of the slang word is kept

parts.note: the macadamia is an Australian nut
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
peeler and rozzer are both old British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman pulls a stopper out of a nut to get at the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers were named after Robert Peel, founder of the London police; rozzer is another old British slang word for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Macrozamia is a genus of Australian cycads, palm-like plants related to the conifers.

clue.text: Parrot-fashion, digitally remastering CD, got lazy, repeating last bit

indicators.note: remastering a recording reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the preceding word is used once more

parts.note: the last letter of lazy, used a second time

explanation.surface: A lazy sound engineer copies a CD parrot-fashion, digitally remastered and looping its last bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot-fashion' looks like rote repetition and 'digitally' like electronics; together they mean arranged like a parrot's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Zygodactyl feet, as in parrots, have two toes pointing forwards and two backwards, so the digits are arranged in parrot style.

clue.text: I stand for a second in game, playful if wary

indicators.note: second in points to the second letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the second letters of game, playful, if and wary

explanation.surface: A player explains what they stand for in a moment of a game: playful but cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word Alfa represents the letter A, so it speaks of itself as standing for that letter.

clue.text: Female comic agreed gags: she had victims in stitches

indicators.note: to gag someone is to cover their mouth, so the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
something comic is absurd and jumbled, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A female comedian whose agreed gags leave her victims in stitches, as in helpless laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In stitches' suggests laughter, fitting a comic, but it means knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Defarge in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities knits a secret register of those condemned to the guillotine.

clue.text: Yellow pack arriving in birthday post

indicators.note: arriving in means coming to sit inside the other piece

parts.note: DOB, date of birth, is a birthday on a form
or is gold or yellow in heraldry
to pack and to jam both mean to cram in

explanation.surface: A yellow parcel turns up in the birthday mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, which fits birthday parcels, but it is an upright post.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the vertical side post of a doorframe, an upright supporting timber.

clue.text: Junk food is hard to get in Dutch province

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase meaning belonging to the province, standing for an adjective

parts.note: fries, chips, are a junk food
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Junk food is hard to come by in a Dutch province.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesish is an old word for Frisian, meaning of or from Friesland, a northern province of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Rare solemnity in dispatching pupils once attendant's released slip

parts.note: OBs, old boys, are former pupils of a school

indicators.note: released means let go, so the following word's letters are set free from the attendant

parts.note: an equerry is an officer attending a member of the royal family
to slip and to err both mean to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Sending pupils away, a school attendant lets a slip of paper go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatching' belongs to the definition: dispatching the dead, a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequy is the rarely used singular of obsequies, the funeral rites performed when someone is laid to rest.

clue.text: Bow, once, before prince related to Byzantine governor

parts.note: a bow is an arc, and once is ex, former, so an ex-arc
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An old bow from a prince's time is linked to a governor of Byzantium.
explanation.definitionFit: Exarchal is the adjective from exarch, the title of a provincial governor in the Byzantine Empire.

clue.text: Strip title from UK, ninth and last in fencing, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the collected letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: the final letter of fencing

explanation.surface: Coming ninth and last in a fencing contest, Britain's team is stripped of its title.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknight is to deprive someone of a knighthood, the honour carrying the title Sir.

clue.text: Religious guru, celebrity, unknown beyond confines of establishment

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the confines are the boundary, so only the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of establishment
z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A celebrity guru is a mysterious figure who stands outside the establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A staretz is a Russian Orthodox elder or holy man revered as a spiritual teacher and adviser.

clue.text: Involving vital element, poisonous with lead removed

indicators.note: the lead is the leading letter, and removing it drops the word's first letter

parts.note: toxic means poisonous

explanation.surface: Something involving a vital element turns poisonous once lead is taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the toxic metal, which suits poisonous, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxic describes conditions or soils containing oxygen, the element living things need to breathe.

clue.text: Do next task, arranging places for drying out

indicators.note: arranging the words means putting their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A to-do list: do the next task, sorting out places for drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drying out' suggests laundry, but it means recovery from drink or drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Detox tanks is slang for centres where people dry out, being weaned off alcohol or drugs under supervision.

clue.text: One used to extract sap keeping stone in beak once

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a juicer is a device for extracting juice
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A tool for drawing sap from a tree keeps a stone stuck in a bird's beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' looks like a bird's bill, but it is British slang for a magistrate or judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Justicer is an archaic word for a judge or one who administers justice, which is what a magistrate does.

clue.text: Purple emblem from board game, one played for longer

parts.note: go is a Japanese board game played with stones
an LP, long-player, is a record played for longer than a single

explanation.surface: A purple emblem comes from a board game which one played for longer.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a golp is a purple roundel, a circular charge painted on a shield.

clue.text: What regularly angry hosts work on by not having relatives for dinner?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another means it is written after it, so work comes second here
to host is to take in guests, so the outer pieces hold the inner ones

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
x means by in measurements, as in two by four
op, opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of angry

explanation.surface: Why would angry hosts work on, refusing to serve family at the dinner table?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a family meal gone sour, but the dinner in question is a cannibal feast. X for by comes from measurements such as two by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Exophagy is cannibalism in which people eat only those outside their own tribe or kin group, never their relations.

clue.text: Stand up for Scotland? Government department not getting in way

indicators.note: not getting in means the two-letter word in is left out of the department

parts.note: a ministry is a government department
st, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A campaigner asks who will stand up for Scotland when a government department won't get in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' looks like defend, but means failing to turn up for a date; 'for Scotland' marks it as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistryst is a Scots verb meaning to break an engagement or fail to keep an appointment with someone.

clue.text: Vulture, one flying through area for last of carrion

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece is swapped in instead of the other

parts.note: a zone is an area

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of carrion
a pilot is someone who flies an aircraft

explanation.surface: A vulture flies through an area in search of carrion.
explanation.walkthrough: PILOT replaces the N in ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Zopilote is the Mexican Spanish name for a smaller American vulture, such as the turkey buzzard.
